cards.head: New York City's pension chief asked AI company Anthropic to delay its share sale.
cards.body: Mark Levine, the city's top money official, wants Anthropic's safety checks set out first. He cannot block the share sale, and Anthropic has not answered yet.

report_refs.excerpt: New York City's comptroller has urged Anthropic to delay its planned stock market listing until it deals with AI safety concerns.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / AI debt fear
cards.head: Insurance against tech firms failing to repay debt hit record prices on AI fears.
cards.body: Data centre operator CoreWeave suffered most, as investors worry AI borrowers cannot pay. Reuters says its price means over a 64% risk of not paying in five years.

report_refs.excerpt: The cost of insuring against defaults by big technology borrowers hit record highs as investors rushed to protect themselves from AI debt risks.

cards.cat: Security and cyber / G7 cyber drill
cards.head: Finance chiefs of the rich G7 nations agreed to practice for an AI cyber attack.
cards.body: Satsuki Katayama, Japan's finance minister, said the drills will test responses and update manuals. The plan follows a warning from the International Monetary Fund, but no dates are set.

report_refs.excerpt: Finance leaders of the G7 group of rich countries have agreed to run practice exercises on how to respond to an AI-driven cyber attack on the financial system.

cards.head: TSMC is in talks to join Tesla chief Elon Musk's planned Texas chip plant.
cards.body: TSMC, the largest contract chip maker, said any such plant must be run by TSMC. Musk has said his own companies will build and run it, and nothing is signed.

report_refs.excerpt: TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, said it is in talks to join Elon Musk's planned Terafab chip complex in Texas, as long as TSMC runs the factory.

cards.head: Apple's boss said Apple will look at every option to beat a memory chip shortage.
cards.body: John Ternus, Apple's chief executive, called the shortage a serious crisis but named no supplier. Korean paper Chosun Ilbo reads this as room for Chinese chips, which US senators oppose.

report_refs.excerpt: Apple's new chief executive John Ternus said Apple will look at every option to ease the memory chip shortage, which could include Chinese-made memory.

cards.head: Volvo plans hands-free driving on local roads, built on chip maker Nvidia's AI.
cards.body: The system would handle traffic lights and turns, but drivers must watch the road. Volvo only promises it before 2030 and has not named which models come first.

report_refs.excerpt: Volvo plans to give its cars Tesla-style hands-free driving on local roads, using Nvidia's AI technology.

cards.head: Car maker Faraday Future launched a small humanoid robot for developers at $2,490.
cards.body: A $299 teaching version is aimed at schools. But the robot walks very slowly, and only 100 are made at first.

report_refs.excerpt: Faraday Future and its robotics partner launched two low-priced humanoid robots, one at $2,490 and a tiny one at $299, aimed at developers and schools.

cards.cat: Models and tools / Meta on Macs
cards.head: Meta released a very large AI model that anyone can download to run on Macs.
cards.body: Meta says Muse Spark Open beats other free-to-download models, based on its own tests. It needs at least 1 terabyte of memory and works best on Apple's Mac Studio.

report_refs.excerpt: Meta has released Muse Spark Open, a very large open-weight AI model built to run on Apple's Mac computers.

cards.head: OpenAI's ChatGPT can now read the tabs you have open in Google's Chrome browser.
cards.body: An updated Chrome add-on lets ChatGPT compare open pages, like three sofas you might buy. Its Work mode can even fill in forms and send messages; no safeguards were described.

report_refs.excerpt: OpenAI has upgraded its ChatGPT Chrome extension so ChatGPT can read the tabs a user already has open and, in its Work mode, act on them.

cards.head: Google made a key quantum computer part with fewer errors, on a real chip.
cards.body: Google's team got about 40 times fewer errors in these parts, in one small test. Making them the old way was expected to use up to 95% of a machine.

report_refs.excerpt: Google's quantum team has shown on real hardware a way to make the special quantum building blocks that error-corrected computers need with far less error and far fewer qubits.

cards.head: OpenAI's coding agent got all but one of 50 unpublished physics problems right.
cards.body: Each answer cost under $3, in a test built by Harvard and Google DeepMind researchers. The authors say AI still lacks the taste to choose good problems.

report_refs.excerpt: A new test of 50 unpublished theoretical physics problems found that OpenAI's GPT-6-Astra coding agent solved 49 of them, at an average cost of under $3 each.

cards.head: A US regulator ordered OpenAI and Anthropic to hand over AI safety incident files.
cards.body: The Federal Trade Commission, which protects consumers, also wants their privacy policies and safeguards. A spokesperson confirmed the demands, which are not a finding of wrongdoing.

report_refs.excerpt: The US Federal Trade Commission has demanded documents from OpenAI and Anthropic about safety incidents involving their AI models.

cards.head: US regulators cleared an AI tool that estimates if early breast cancer will return.
cards.body: Made by SimBioSys, it reads an existing breast scan and lab results before surgery. It was tested only on past records, and insurers do not cover it yet.

report_refs.excerpt: An AI tool that estimates whether early breast cancer will come back has won FDA clearance and can give the estimate before surgery.

cards.cat: Society and education / Fed AI hiring
cards.head: Some US firms are hiring fewer people after investing in AI, the Fed reports.
cards.body: The Federal Reserve's latest business survey heard this in five of its twelve regions. Most regions saw little job change, and the survey rests on what bosses told it.

report_refs.excerpt: The US Federal Reserve's latest business survey says some companies in five of its twelve regions have cut back or delayed hiring after investing in AI.

cards.head: MIT researchers left AI agents alone on a virtual island, and one built a temple.
cards.body: Each agent got a lobster body and thirty hours with no instructions. Six found a throwing trick nobody had coded, which the researchers compare to animal play.

report_refs.excerpt: MIT researchers left thirteen AI agents alone on a virtual island for thirty hours and watched them stack blocks, build temples and invent their own games.

entries.head: Anthropic let six outside safety testers work inside the company with staff-level access.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic has given six researchers from the independent testing group METR the same kind of access to its models and internal tools as its own staff, and METR can publish what it finds.

entries.head: Drug maker AstraZeneca hired AI firm insitro to hunt for liver and heart drug targets.

report_refs.excerpt: AstraZeneca has signed a deal with AI drug-discovery company insitro worth up to $1.5 billion, though only $40 million is paid up front.

entries.head: Cameroon banned nursery and primary school pupils from using AI chatbots like ChatGPT.

report_refs.excerpt: Cameroon has banned pupils in nursery and primary schools from using generative AI tools such as ChatGPT.

entries.head: Microsoft finished training a giant AI model it says needs far less computing power.

report_refs.excerpt: Microsoft says it has finished training MAI-Base-2, a 2.8 trillion-parameter AI model it claims needs far less computing power than a leading Chinese rival to reach the same results.

cards.head: Borrowing for AI costs more: debt fears hit records as chip demand stays strong.
cards.body: Insuring CoreWeave's data centre debt hit a record as chipmaker TSMC made record profit. Watch Meta's results on 21 October: less spending means weaker demand.

report_refs.excerpt: The cost of insuring against defaults by big technology borrowers hit record highs as investors rushed to protect themselves from AI debt risks.
Chip and memory stocks suffered a second day of heavy selling, wiping more than $1 trillion off the value of the biggest names this week.

BigGo Finance reports that investors this week sold off the bonds of CoreWeave, a US company that rents out AI data centres, pushing the yield on its 2032 notes to almost 15%, in what the Financial Times describes as a 'Darwin moment' for AI borrowers.

Livemint reports that C.C. Wei, chief executive of TSMC, said demand for its advanced chips is extremely robust and that it wants every piece of business it can get, while CNBC reports a fierce battle among Nvidia, Apple and Broadcom for its factory space.
Some investors are reportedly weighing a lower valuation of about $1.5 trillion for Anthropic's planned stock market debut, down from roughly $2 trillion, after its revenue growth slowed.

cards.notice: General news and commentary. Not financial advice or an investment recommendation.

If this adds value to your day, share it with someone who should know. Thank you, and see you tomorrow.
